summary: FieldShift helps farmers explore crop rotations as heat, rainfall and water availability change. A farmer selects a location, enters known soil and irrigation details, and sets priorities. The app retrieves historical NASA POWER daily climate data, calculates seasonal climate context and a modelled crop water deficit, then compares rule-based rotations for four pilot regions. Each alternative shows its crop sequence, feasibility checks, component scores, sources, trade-offs and missing information. Farmers can compare their existing rotation and run clearly labelled hypothetical dry, hot and irrigation-reduction stress tests. The world map provides climate context outside the pilots without claiming locally validated crop advice. FieldShift supports discussion with a local adviser. It does not forecast yield, profit, groundwater savings or soil improvement.
details:
HOW IT WORKS

FieldShift starts with a point on the map or farm coordinates. It retrieves daily temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, humidity and wind from the official NASA POWER API. The app preserves the request URL, units, dates and missing-data counts. Monthly and seasonal summaries are calculated from that historical record. The climate data are gridded context, not measurements from the farmer's field.

The farmer can enter soil texture, pH, organic carbon, drainage, previous crops and available water. Unknown values remain unknown. For four pilot regions (Punjab, Iowa, Andalusia and semi-arid India), a deterministic engine builds crop sequences from source-linked calendars and rotation rules. It checks known hard constraints, then compares supported water, climate, soil and diversity indicators using editable priority weights. Each plan exposes the checks and methods behind its scores. The farmer can add a current rotation to the comparison. Dry, hot and irrigation-reduction settings are hypothetical stress tests, not forecasts.

WHY IT MATTERS

The tool makes the reason for a recommendation visible and lets the farmer see how a change in available water or priorities affects alternatives. The globe makes historical climate data accessible worldwide; rotation advice is limited to the four configured pilot catalogues. Economic scores and numerical soil-improvement claims are withheld because the needed crop-level evidence and local calibration are not verified. FieldShift is a decision-support prototype; agronomist review, farmer testing and field calibration remain necessary.

BUILT WITH

Python, Streamlit, pandas, NumPy, SciPy and Plotly. The public source, test fixtures and scientific assumptions are at https://github.com/sagar25446-prog/Nasa-Hacakathon . The deterministic offline test suite reports 270 passed and five skipped optional integration tests.
